title: Lambda: handler, runtimes, layers and the deployment package

videos.script: A Lambda function is easy to picture as a program that starts for a request and stops after it. {{env}} That picture costs money and time, so this lesson replaces it. Lambda starts an environment and imports your file once. Then it calls one function in it for every event. {{handler}} You will write that function, a handler, and run it for real on your laptop. The runtime is the one AWS publishes as a container image, with a small emulator inside. You send it events with curl, and read the same log lines Lambda writes. {{package}} Then the function goes into moto as a zip file, with a role, a version and an update. moto keeps the record and none of the limits. So you will see exactly where AWS would say no. {{layers}} Next comes a layer: shared code that Lambda unpacks into a directory of its own. You will break a function by leaving it out. Then you fix it by mounting it where Lambda would. {{arm}} Last, the runtime itself. It has an end date, and a choice of processor. Arm is a fifth cheaper per second, and the lesson works out what that is worth in a month.
